sentences.text: Tropidosteus curvatus is a large, extinct arthrodire placoderm known from a slender, forty-two-centimeter-long arched median dorsal plate.
The sides of this dorsal plate meet at an angle of sixty to ninety degrees, suggesting the live animal had a humped appearance.
The genus Tropidosteus was described by Gross in 1933, and the only known species is Tropidosteus curvatus, which was also named by Gross that same year.

Tropidosteus belongs to the class Placodermi and is placed within the family Holonematidae because its median dorsal plate is similar to those of Rhenonema and Belemnacanthus. The parent group of the genus is the family Holonematidae.
This animal lived during the Givetian stage of the Devonian period and was found in the Middle Devonian Crinoidenmergel stratum of Rheinland, Germany.
Denison (1978) questioned the placement of Tropidosteus in the family Holonematidae because its dorsal plate lacks the ridged ornamentation considered a key diagnostic trait.
